sentences.text: Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Surender

MACMA.Nos.1329 and 1137 of 2012
Common Judgment

:
1. M.A.C.M.A.No.1329 of 2012 is filed by the insurance company questioning the compensation granted by the Chairman, Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-V Additional District Judge at Karimnagar in MVOP No.214 of 2007, dated 13.05.2011.
2. M.A.C.M.A.No.1137 of 2012 is filed by the insurance company questioning the compensation granted by the Chairman, Motor Vehicle Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-V Additional District Judge at Karimnagar in MVOP No.213 of 2007, dated 13.05.2011.
3. The deceased in MVOP No.214 of 2007 and the injured in MVOP No.213 of 2007 were traveling in the Ambassador car which was driven by the husband of the injured in MVOP No.213 of 2007.

While they were traveling in the car, when they reached the place near Shanigaram village, lorry which was coming in the opposite direction, drove it in rash and negligent manner and to avoid accident with the said lorry, the driver of the Ambassador car lost control and the car and hit a tree.
4. Both the petitions were filed under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act.
In the Tribunal, having considered both the petitions, directed payment of compensation by the insurer of the Ambassador car, in which they were traveling.

5. The main ground urged by the learned Counsel appearing for the insurance company is that the policy is 'Act Policy' and will not cover the persons traveling in the car since they are gratuitous passengers.
Accordingly, Awards of the trial Court both OPs are liable to be dismissed.

6. Learned counsel relied on the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of United India Insurance Co., Ltd., v. Tilak Singh and others (2006 ACJ 1441) and also the Judgment passed by this Court in MACMA No.670 of 2021 dated 08.06.2022 and argued that the insurer cannot be made liable for payment of compensation.

sentences.text:
He also relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Division Bench in the case of Branch Manager, United India Insurance Co., Ltd., Kamareddy, Nizamabad District v.
Kondakotla Saroja and others (2008 (5) ALD 288(DB) and argued that in all the cases, the liability of the insurance company was set aside when it was found that the claim was made on behalf of gratuitous passengers.

Kondakotla Saroja and others (2008 (5) ALD 288(DB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Learned counsel further relied on the orders of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sk.Wasimoddin v. The United India Insurance Company Limited in SLP to Appeal (C )
No.16628 of 2019, dated 29.02.2024, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court had referred the question to the Larger Bench.

The question raised is as follows:

sentences.text: "However, the question as to whether the third party includes all other persons other than the insured, who is the first party and the insurer, who is the second party.
Therefore, all other persons who are neither the insured nor the insurer will be third party and will be covered by the Act Only Policy, we have prima facie reservation about the view expressed.

Such question is required to be determined authoritatively."
7.

On the other hand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the claimants would submit that in the Three Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shivaji and another v. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., and others (2018 (5) ALD 135 (SC)), the Hon'ble Supreme Court while dealing with the petition filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act held that the factum of 'Fault' cannot be considered since Section 163-A of the Act introduced for granting compensation without proof of 'fault'.

entities.text: Shivaji and another v. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., and others (2018 (5) ALD 135 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel also relied on the judgment of this Court in the case of United India Insurance Co., Ltd., Hyderabad v. Syed Rehmath Ali and others (2020 (3) ALD 108 (TS), wherein compensation was granted to the injured in the car though the policy was 'Act Policy'.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co., Ltd., Hyderabad v. Syed Rehmath Ali and others (2020 (3) ALD 108 (TS)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said judgment, the deceased was not the driver of the car but sitting in the car and accordingly, this Court found that though it is an 'Act Policy', liability arose on the insurance company to pay compensation.

At this juncture, learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that this Court in Syed Rehmath Ali's case (supra), has not considered the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Tilak Singh's case (supra).

8. The Tribunal, on the basis of the judgment of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Co.,
Ltd., Secunderabad v. Palamoni Suresh and another (2010(3) TAC 480 (A.P), this Court held that if a private vehicle is allowed to carry persons other than owner or driver as per conditions of registration, all such persons come within the expression 'third party' and accordingly granted compensation.

entities.text:
New India Assurance Co.,
Ltd., Secunderabad v. Palamoni Suresh and another (2010(3) TAC 480 (A.P)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Divergent views are taken in the judgments regarding the passengers in a vehicle, which is covered by 'Act Policy', whether they are gratuitous passengers or third parties.
Further, as stated above, the question being referred to Larger Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, this Court deems it appropriate to uphold the order of the Tribunal in granting compensation.

The enactment of Motor Vehicles Act directing payment of compensation to victims being beneficial legislation and the claimants are denied compensation since 2005, this Court deems it appropriate to direct for payment of compensation as ordered by the Tribunal.
Compensation shall be paid to the claimants in accordance with the conditions laid down by the Tribunal.
10. Accordingly, both the Appeals are dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.

Consequently,
miscellaneous applications, if any, pending, shall stand closed.
